enquiry: Our NIR moisture model was built for wheat flour. We now also mill rye and oat flour, and our instrument supplier says the same model will work because water absorbs the same way in every flour. We would like to start using it on the new flours next week.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today with moisture control on the mill, and what decision will the real-time moisture value drive for rye and oat flour?
clarification_questions.why: Clarifies the stakeholder pain and the consequence of a wrong moisture reading on the new flours.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Pain and decision unknown; treat the model as unvalidated for release decisions until the expert confirms the purpose.

clarification_questions.question: Is moisture the only target for rye and oat flour, and what moisture range do these flours typically reach in your process?
clarification_questions.why: Determines the level range that a calibration must cover and whether the wheat model's range applies.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Moisture level for the new flours unknown; lab screening establishes the range needed.

clarification_questions.question: How is the rye and oat flour presented to the sensor (bulk, spout, sample cup), and is it the same presentation used for the wheat calibration?
clarification_questions.why: Particle size and packing change NIR scattering and can invalidate a transferred calibration.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Presentation unknown and assumed different from the wheat calibration until verified.

clarification_questions.question: How much do rye and oat flour vary between mill batches, in particle size, composition and temperature, compared with the wheat flour used for the calibration?
clarification_questions.why: Batch variation determines whether a single model can be robust across the new flours.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Variation unknown; the wheat model is not assumed valid for the new flours.

clarification_questions.question: Where is the NIR analyzer installed relative to the measuring point, and is the same instrument and fibre setup used for all flours?
clarification_questions.why: Installation geometry affects the spectra and whether the existing calibration transfers.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation assumed identical to the wheat setup until confirmed.

clarification_questions.question: What reference laboratory method is used for moisture, what is its accuracy, and can reference samples be taken for rye and oat flour?
clarification_questions.why: Without reference data on the new flours, the model's accuracy cannot be checked.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No reference data for the new flours; a lab comparison on representative samples is required before use.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy on moisture does the process need for rye and oat flour, and by when must the sensor be in use?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the acceptance criterion and whether a transfer, a new calibration or a different method is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Accuracy requirement unknown; no release on the new flours until it is defined.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: S01 p.10 does say NIR bands overlap and suggest chemometrics, but it does not say the models depend on the calibration samples; that specific claim is not on the cited page. Fix: Limit the claim to: broad overlapping NIR bands suggest chemometrics for quantitative and qualitative analysis, or cite a page that states calibration dependence.

different_context: S02 p.12 shows SNV-corrected NIR spectra of starch, flour and sugar and a water-drop drying demo on wood in an IoT sensor context; it does not show a moisture example for bulk flour with a customised calibration. The transfer to bulk flour is not stated on the page. Fix: Describe the page as a wood-surface water-drying demo with NIR spectra of starch, flour and sugar, and state that a flour moisture calibration is not shown there.

not_supported: The cited pages list NIR diffuse reflection probes for powders (r8, r9, r10) but the claim cites many unrelated rows (MIR, Raman, UV-Vis, fluorimetry) and the page text does not establish that the existing NIR interface is diffuse reflection suited to the client's powders. Fix: Cite only the NIR diffuse reflection rows (TABLE:r8, TABLE:r9, TABLE:r10) and state that they are generic suitability ratings for powders, not confirmation of the client's existing interface.

overstated: S02 p.6 gives Vis-NIR silica transmission as 350–2400 nm, which covers much of the NIR range, but the claim 'covers most of the NIR range' is a general judgment; the page also notes values are transcribed from a figure to be checked, and the range is not confirmed for the client's link. Fix: State that the Vis-NIR silica transmission range on S02 p.6 (350–2400 nm) overlaps much of the NIR band, and that the exact values must be checked against the figure and the actual fiber.

not_supported: S02 p.6 lists transmission ranges only; it does not classify fibers as full-range or partial for NIR, so the 'full range' and 'partial' labels are not stated on the cited page. Fix: Report the transmission ranges from S02 p.6 and derive the NIR overlap explicitly, noting that the full/partial classification is an inference.

not_supported: DOCX §5 says calibration is matrix-specific but does not mention wheat, rye, oat or moisture bias; the specific risk is not on the cited page. Fix: Cite the matrix-specific calibration statement from DOCX §5 as the general basis and state the wheat/rye/oat bias as an inference to test.

overstated: S02 p.12 is a demo slide with no validation data, so it can support 'not validation' but the claim's wording about the slide being 'an example' is consistent; however the page does not itself state that it is not validation for these flours, so the stated certainty rests on the reviewer's judgment. Fix: Phrase as: the S02 p.12 demo is an illustrative example with no validation data reported on the slide.
